title: [performance] nightly 023's busy-minute limit from the measured spread of unchanged loop code: BUSY_MAX 9,100 -> 10,500 (the highest of 23 quiet runs, 9,549, plus 10%), so unchanged code passes and a step that adds work still fails
prompt:
Spawn, objective 243 [performance] (an owner change on rsi/, committed by the lead; no fleet task; the lead's 05:2x ask, 2026-11-20, from the nightly RED on 84dcd333; author rev-i; readers rev-g first, rev-j second): nightly 023's busy-minute limit is derived from the measured spread of unchanged loop code, so unchanged code passes it and a step that adds work still fails it.

Why. The nightly went RED on main 84dcd333: 023.sh's busy minute cost 9,132 and 9,124 table scans against BUSY_MAX 9,100. The last green, 38c3a263, ran 8,935. Fleet task landings are held until the nightly is green or flaky.
- No landing added the scans. On a quiet host, 38c3a263 and 84dcd333 alternating (3+3, the same 023.sh) gave 8,805-9,051 and 8,801-9,173: the ranges interleave and the means differ by 0.9%.
  - Every table and the transaction count moved together, with scans per transaction unchanged, so the head runs more of the same transactions, not a new or costlier query.
  - The loop code 023 reaches changed in the range only by paths it does not take: t515u's fold (model judge only), 223's retire, 234's integrator.
  - Live 2f0d2198 (239's steal step) ran 8,910.
- The quiet nightly re-run on 5e416443 failed both its candidate and its base (9,034-9,300, 0 gates beside). It was SKIPPED, and the red cannot end on its own.
- 9,100 was the highest of 22 runs on 2026-11-08/09 (8,282) plus 10%. Unchanged code now costs 8,801-9,549, so the limit sits inside the spread.

What changes (owner part, rsi/scenarios/nightly/023.sh only):
1. BUSY_MAX 9,100 → 10,500: the highest of 23 quiet runs of unchanged loop code (9,549, on 5e416443) plus 10%, rounded down to the hundred. This is the same rule as before, measured again.
2. The (3) failure message names that derivation (23 runs, 9,549, plus 10%), not the old 22 runs and 8,282.
3. The header's BUSY_MAX paragraph says:
   - the 23 runs and their range;
   - that the cost crept over the old limit with no landing behind it (the A/B above);
   - that the limit is derived again, by the same rule, when unchanged code reaches it;
   - what it still catches, now with 243's two step-added mutants, and what it does not.
Nothing else in 023.sh changes: the setup, the idle checks (1)-(2), IDLE_MAX 150, and every timing check of (3).

Files: rsi/scenarios/nightly/023.sh, rsi/backlog/243.json.

- The A/B of 38c3a263 against 84dcd333 (3+3) and the run on 2f0d2198 are the evidence that no landing added the scans.
